interactions.declared_note: Chosen on product grounds: chocolate with its most common partners.
interactions.rule: Retain an interaction only if its 95% CI excludes 0 and leave-one-out R² does not worsen relative to the main model.

results.reason: design matrix is rank deficient: some terms are exact linear combinations of others and cannot be estimated separately
an observation has leverage 1 (it alone identifies a term), so its leave-one-out residual, and with it leave-one-out R² and HC3 standard errors, is undefined

profiles.support_rule: within 1 attribute of at least one real candy
profiles.range_note: CI and prediction interval bounds are capped to 0-100; 'capped' marks profiles where the linear model's range left that scale.
profiles.tie_note: A profile is tied with the primary profile when the 95% CI of the predicted gap between the two includes zero.

recommendation.rule: The primary profile is the best supported profile made only of drivers: attributes whose positive effect survives the multiple-testing correction. Every other attribute is a design choice the data does not decide.

cookie_vs_gummy.note: Predicted with the model that includes the gummy attribute, at the same sugar and price level as the profiles. Every cookie candy in the data is chocolate, so a non-chocolate cookie cannot be assessed. These scores come from the gummy model, so the chocolate score differs slightly from the primary profile's, which uses the main model; compare products within this section only.

logit.effects_note: Average marginal effects in win-rate points: discrete 0-to-1 change for attributes, mean derivative for sugar and price level. Intervals rescale the logit-scale intervals by a fixed factor, ignoring that factor's own uncertainty.

data_notes: 85 market entries in the source data; the 2 coins (One dime and One quarter) are survey decoys, not candies, and are excluded, leaving 83 candies.
Including the coins moves no attribute or level coefficient by more than 1.6 points of win rate.
Win rate is the share of roughly 269,000 head-to-head matchups a candy won. Win rate measures relative preference, not sales or satisfaction.
Sugar level and price level are percentile ranks within the dataset (0 to 1), not grams of sugar or prices.
The source column 'peanutyalmondy' (spelled 'peanutalmondy' in the source documentation) is analysed as the peanut/almond attribute.
Only 7 candies have nougat and 7 have crisped rice/wafer/cookie, so those effects carry wide intervals.
Gummy is a hand-coded attribute (11 of 83 candies; 11 judgement calls flagged), used to test the gummy effect and to compare a gummy with chocolate products.
